reference: VFG053958(gb|WP_012457177.1) (porU) type IX secretion system sortase PorU [T9SS (VF1427) - Effector delivery system (VFC0086)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: T9SS is a protein secretion machinery unique to the Bacteroidetes-Chlorobi-Fibrobacteres superphylum, which plays crucial roles in bacterial pathogenesis and gliding motility.
structure: T9SS composed of at least 18 components and is formed of a large translocon complex and a smaller attachment complex. The translocon complex spans  both the inner and outer membranes while the attachment complex is located in the outer membrane. In the translocon complex, PorL assembles into a pentamer within the inner membrane, and generates proton motive force which facilitates the rotation of a PorM dimer in the periplasm. Twelve PorL/PorM subcomplexes arrange into a tubular structure which spans the periplasm and interacts with a 50 nm ring formed of PorN and PorK on the periplasmic side  of the outer membrane. The outer membrane protein PorG is covalently bonded to PorK and may help tether multiple copies of the attachment  complex  (PorU/PorV/PorQ/PorZ)  above  the  PorK/PorN ring on the extracellular surface. The translocon pore protein, Sov, associates with the outer membrane PorV, the periplasmic lipoprotein PorW, and the periplasmic protein SkpA, which also anchors Sov to the PorK/PorN ringprotein;All T9SS cargo proteins are translocated across the inner membrane (IM) by the Sec translocon due to their N-terminal signal sequence and are then recruited by the T9SS for secretion across the outer membrane (OM) by their structurally conserved C-terminal domain (CTD) sequence.
function_description: Transports over 30 virulence-associated proteins, including gingipains, hemagglutinins, and peptidylarginine deiminase, an enzyme potentially linked to rheumatoid arthritis.

reference: VFG053977(gb|WP_043876339.1) (rgpA) Arg-gingipain RgpA [RgpA (VF1428) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: Gingipains belong to cysteine proteinases of the peptidase family C25;The cell-surface proteases RgpA, RgpB, and Kgp, collectively known as the gingipains, account for 85% of the general proteolytic activity exhibited by this organism; RgpB maintains its activity at a higher pH(pH 9.0), whereas RgpA is most effective at a neutral pH of 7.5;The gingipain gene products are initially expressed as inactive zymogens and require post-translational modifications for activation.
function_description: Selectively hydrolyzing peptide bonds at the carboxyl termini of arginine residues to facilitate nutrient acquisition while promoting bacterial invasion into subgingival regions, immune evasion, and

accession: RgpA assembles into a non-covalent complex with HA domains, forming HRgpA. Kgp, which also includes HA domains, associates with HRgpA to form a highly potent HRgpA-Kgp proteolytic complex. These HA segments are crucial for hemoglobin binding, hemagglutination, and P.gingivalisPrevotella intermedia coaggregation, facilitating periodontal biofilm formation; alters the host immune responses by targeting TREM-1, CD14 (LPS receptor), and complement regulators like CD46 and C5aR;potent inducer of neutrophil extracellular trap formation (NETosis) in human neutrophils; RgpA interacts with gingival keratinocytes and dendritic cells, initiating the release of proinflammatory cytokines via the EGFR-PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. This inflammatory response promotes bone resorption and facilitates the expansion of pathobionts, thereby worsening periodontitis progression and potentially impacting systemic conditions associated with periodontal pathogens;implicated in disruption of the bloodbrain barrier, leading to neurodegeneration through dysregulation of the Ddx3x/Mfsd2a/Cav-1 signaling axis;degrades tight junction proteins such as Zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) and occludin in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells to compromise blood-brain barrier integrity;targets the insulin-binding region of insulin receptor (INSR), disrupting its function and impairing insulin signaling, contributing to insulin resistance (IR) in the liver, muscle, and adipose tissue.

reference: VFG053978(gb|WP_012458292.1) (rgpB) Arg-gingipain RgpB [RgpB (VF1429) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: RgpB is not adhesin-associated and is a monomer anchored to the outer membrane; RgpB lacks the hemagglutinin domains and shares over 97% identity with the protease domain of RgpA. Despite the virtually identical protease domains of the same catalytic capacity for the Arg-Xaa peptide bone, these two proteases differentially impact neutrophil responses. Unlike RgpA, neutrophils exposed to RgpB do not undergo apoptosis and have a limited or delayed NETosis response. RgpB degrades neutrophil granule proteins and serine proteases, reducing phagosomal microbicidal capacity;RgpB is considered to be a more clinically important marker. RgpB interacts with a variety of host proteins, resulting in a robust inflammatory response in periodontal tissues and accelerating the progression of periodontitis. Conversely, RgpA displays relatively low activity with regard to tissue destruction and the induction of inflammatory responses.
function_description: A proteolytic tool for the degradation of proteinaceous nutrients to P. gingivalis for growth, and essential for the processing of fimbrial proteins to facilitate bacterial attachment and adhesion to the host;facilitates bacterial evasion of the host immune response by cleaving surface receptors and cytokines degradation.
mechanism: Cysteine proteases that hydrolyze peptide bonds at the carbonyl groups of arginine (Arg-Xaa).

function_description: Degrades host proteins and tissues, aids in immune evasion, enhances bacterial adherence to host cells and tissues, and facilitates iron acquisition and the maturation of other virulence factors.

reference: VFG053980(gb|WP_012457396.1) (mfa1) fimbria major subunit Mfa1 [Mfa1 fimbriae (VF1431) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: Type V pili are unique to Gram-negative bacteria belonging to the class Bacteroidia in the phylum Bacteroidetes;P. gingivalis possesses type V pili that are either of the long (0.31.6 µm), major Fim pilus type or the short (80120 nm), minor Mfa type, thereby the Mfa1 fimbriae, also termed minor or short fimbriae.
structure: Contains five protein components: Mfa1-5;Mfa1 constitutes the shaft, Mfa2 the anchor, and Mfa3-5 the tip proteins of Mfa1 fimbria; In the first step, the fimbrial protein is transported over the inner membrane via the general secretory pathway, after which the signal peptide is removed by signal peptidase II. The cleaved protein is linked to a lipid in the membrane via its N-terminal cysteine, resulting in a lipoprotein precursor. Finally, RgpA/B, cleave the protein into its mature form.  Hence the mature forms of Mfa1, Mfa3 and Mfa4 start immediately following an Rgp cleavage site at Arg49, Arg43 and Arg54 respectively. The anchor protein Mfa2 does not have an Rgp or a Kgp recognition site and apparently continues to be linked to the membrane via its N-terminal cysteine and no evidence of N-terminal trimming has been reported for the tip protein Mfa5.
function_description: Crucial for attachment to other bacteria in the oral biofilm and to the host cells.
mechanism: Mfa1 interacts with a specific region of the C-terminal domain of the streptococcal SspB/A adhesins and dendritic cell-specific ICAM-3 grabbing nonintegrin (DC-SIGN) of dendritic cells; Mfa1-expressing strains have been shown to invade monocytes and promote their differentiation to myeloid-derived dendritic suppressor cells (MDDSCs). MDDSCs induce immune tolerance through increased FOXP3+ Treg responses. reference: VFG053991(gb|WP_012457400.1) (ragA) RagA/SusC family TonB-linked outer membrane protein [RagAB (VF1434) - Nutritional/Metabolic factor (VFC0272)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: The ragAB locus exhibits considerable heterogeneity. Sequence variations of up to 30% in ragA and as high as 4847% in ragB were observed. A new concept is emerging that different variants of the ragAB operon allow P. gingivalis strains to forage on different sets of peptides generated by degradation of host proteins;Genes ragA and ragB are co-transcribed, and their expression is highly interdependent.
structure: RagA is a 22-stranded beta-barrel, and RagB is the corresponding 4-TPR lid, together forming a TonB-dependent system acting as a 'pedal bin';Crystallography revealed the RagAB structure as a heterotetrameric complex acting as a double 'pedal bin' with monomers opening independently, enabling the uptake of the gingipain-cleaved proteinaceous nutrients/peptides.
function_description: RagA and RagB are major components of the outer membrane of P. gingivalis and have been linked with virulence because of their contribution to subcutaneous lesion development, epithelial cell invasion, and efficient growth of the pathogen by acting as a transport system for nutrients.
mechanism: The RagAB transport complex has been implicated in oligopeptide acquisition, essential for a proteolytic bacterium.

reference: VFG053993(gb|WP_012458403.1) (PGN_RS07665) sialidase family protein [Sialidase (VF1436) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: NA
function_description: A type of glycosyl hydrolase enzyme involved in P. gingivalis cell surface structures, hydrophobicity, biofilm  formation, resistance to complement and neutrophil killing, and host immune responses.
mechanism: Sialidase may affect LPS and lipids, in turn altering the surface hydrophobicity properties of P. gingivalis. Sialidase mutants with more hydrophilic surfaces had poor biofilm formation; Sialidase removes sialic acids from host serum and several complement factors such as C1q, C4, and fH and thus likely protects P. gingivalis from serum killing by disarming key complement factors (e.g., C1q and C4) via desialylation; Sialidase may affect P. gingivalis-induced pro-inflammation via LPS sialylation;assists P. gingivalis in escaping the IL-12-mediated clearance in macrophages by exploiting CR3.

reference: VFG053994(gb|WP_004585202.1) (serB) protein-serine phosphatase SerB [SerB (VF1437) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: A haloacid dehalogenase (HAD) family serine protease.
function_description: Serine phosphatase SerB induces dephosphorylation of cofilin, and that active cofilin is required for optimal invasion into gingival epithelial cells; inhibits of NF-kappaB activation to manipulate host inflammatory pathways.
mechanism: A central feature of P. gingivalis pathogenicity is dysregulation of innate immunity at the gingival epithelial interface, including suppression of IL-8 production by epithelial cells. SerB dephosphorylates the serine 538 residue of the p65 subunit of NF-kappaB. The formation of active p65-p65 homodimers is thus prevented, and consequently synthesis of neutrophil chemokine IL-8 is suppressed.

reference: VFG053995(gb|WP_012458492.1) (hagA) hemagglutinin A [HagA (VF1438) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: One large class of virulence factors that P. gingivalis produces are the hemagglutinins. Multiple hemagglutinins have been identified in P. gingivalis; This group of proteins plays an essential role in a number of aspects of the infectious process, in particular with regards to nutrient acquisition. Porphyromonas  gingivalis is a heme auxotroph and does not possess the enzymes required for heme biosynthesis. In addition, the lack of a siderophore scavenging system means that it must rely on alternative mechanisms of iron uptake.
structure: A large surface-associated protein of predicted molecular mass of 283.3 kDa containing multiple contiguous direct repeats (hemagglutinin A repeat HArep) of 440-456 amino acids, with hemagglutinin activity for each of the repeats. The multiple repeat units might be involved in antigenic variation.
function_description: Required for colonization and invasion of host cells; plays a key role in facilitating the acquisition of heme through erythrocyte binding. Hemagglutinins facilitate the absorption of heme by P. gingivalis, allowing the proteolytic gingipains to release the heme moiety from the hemoglobin molecule, which is then internalized by the HmuY/HmuR dual component uptake system.

reference: VFG053996(gb|WP_012458742.1) (husD) Hus system protein HusD [Hus system (VF1442) - Nutritional/Metabolic factor (VFC0272)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: NA
structure: Hus system consists of 4 proteins (HusA, HusB, HusC, and HusD) and is encoded on the hus operon; HusA is a hemophore-like protein not belonging to the HmuY family or classical hemophores, and HusB is a typical TDR (TonB-dependent outer membrane receptor). Both proteins, like HmuY and HmuR, form a two-component heme/PPIX uptake system. HusC and HusD proteins whose functions are unknown.HusA is a lipoprotein associated with the outer membrane and can be found extr acellularl y as a soluble protein or associated with OMV; HusA binds free heme or heme bound in the ferrous form to albumin; gingipains can degrade the soluble form of HusA, releasing heme, which is in contrast to the high resistance to proteolysis of HmuY  only.
function_description: Hus system may play a greater role in the survival of P. gingivalis in the host environment, especially inside the host cells.

reference: VFG054000(gb|WP_012458344.1) (php1) polysaccharide biosynthesis protein-tyrosine phosphatase Php1 [Php1 (VF1443) - Post-translational modification (VFC0315)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: Regulation of tyrosine phosphorylation in bacteria is mediated mainly by bacterial protein-tyrosine kinases in conjunction with three families of protein-tyrosine phosphatases: 1)the low-molecular-weight phosphatases (LMW-PTPs), a family of small acidic enzymes also found in eukaryotes. 2)the eukaryotic-like phosphatases (PTPs), which are dual-specific phosphatases that also display activity against phosphoserine and phosphothreonine. 3)the DNA polymerase and histidinol phosphate phosphoesterase (PHP) family; PHP family are widespread in Gram-positive bacteria; P. gingivalis has a unique configuration whereby two tyrosine phosphatases (Php1 and Ltp1) can act on a BY kinase (Ptk1);The php1 gene is located immediately downstream of the gene encoding the bacterial tyrosine (BY) kinase Ptk1; Php1 tyrosine phosphatase in P. gingivalis displayed metal ion dependence, primarily for manganese; optimally active at alkaline pH (7.5 to 8.0).
function_description: Required for P. gingivalis exopolysaccharide production and for community development with the antecedent oral biofilm constituent Streptococcus gordonii under nutrient-depleted conditions.

reference: VFG054001(gb|WP_012457551.1) (ltp1) low molecular weight protein-tyrosine-phosphatase [Ltp1 (VF1444) - Post-translational modification (VFC0315)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: Ltp1 is secreted within gingival epithelial cells and translocates to the nucleus; Numerous host-bacteria interactions depend on secreted bacterial LMW-PTP, such as Staphylococcus aureus PtpA, Mycobacterium tuberculosis PtpA and PtpB; The activity of Ltp1, but not Php1, was inhibited by pABA (para-amino benzoic acid) and H2O2.
structure: Ltp1 contains the conserved catalytic motif C(X)5R. The nucleophile cysteine within this phosphotransfer loop is required for phosphatase activity, while the arginine is necessary for substrate binding.
function_description: Contributes to community formation with oral partner species Streptoccus gordonii; required for P. gingivalis to enhance epithelial cell proliferation and migration.
mechanism: Ltp1 can dephosphorylate and inactivate Ptk1. The Php1/Ltp1-Ptk1 axis can control production of the FimA and Mfa1 fimbriae and extracellular polysaccharide (EPS);Ltp1 dephosphorylates PTEN on Y336 leading to proteasomal degradation. A reduction of PTEN levels relieves suppression of PI3K/Akt which upregulates RGCC (Regulator of Growth and Cell Cycle) and Zeb2. Disruption of the Akt1/RGCC signaling axis by Ltp1 facilitates P. gingivalis-induced increases in epithelial cell migration, proliferation, EMT and inflammatory cytokine production.

mechanism: Para-amino benzoic acid (pABA), is both an essential substrate for OCM and an inhibitor of the low molecular weight tyrosine phosphatase Ltp1, which consequently relieves inhibition of its cognate tyrosine kinase, Ptk1. Active Ptk1 is necessary for  secretion  of  gingipains  which  can  provide  amino  acid  substrates  to maintain OCM flux. Diminished pABA levels lead to inhibition of Ptk1 and retention of active gingipains on the cell surface. Among the genes included in the cluster are genes encoding an EC 2.7.8.33, UDP-N-acetylglucosamine-undecaprenyl-phosphate N-acetylglucosaminephosphotransferase (PG0106), EC 5.1.3.14, UDP-N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase (non-hydrolyzing) (PG0120), four predicted glycosyltransferases (PG0110, PG0111, PG0118, and PG0119), two acetyl-transferases (PG0113 and PG0115), and a flippase (PG0117).
function_description: Plays an important function in evasion of the immune response;not a requirement for serum resistance in P. gingivalis.

reference: VFG054066(gb|WP_012458603.1) (hagB) hemagglutinin protein HagB [HagB (VF1439) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: NA
structure: A non-fimbrial adhesion protein on the surface of P. gingivalis; a 49.0 kDa protein composed of 350 amino acid residues with a pI of 8.42.
function_description: Involved in P. gingivalis adhesion to human coronary artery endothelial (HCAE) cells;pro-inflammatory and induces chemokine and cytokine responses in a variety of cells.
mechanism: HagB induces an elevated matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) response in dendritic cells. MMPs are part of a large family of calcium-dependent, zinc containing endopeptidases that play a critical role in the inflammatory response either by modifying proteins post-translationally to promote rapid delivery to other cells or by inactivating these proteins to initiate or terminate the immune process;Both histatin 5 and human beta defensin 3 (HBD3) bind to HagB and both attenuate HagB-induced chemokine and cytokine responses in dendritic cells.

reference: VFG054068(gb|WP_012458605.1) (hagC) hemagglutinin protein HagC [HagC (VF1440) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: The hag genes can be subdivided into two distinct families; hagA, hagD, and hagE which possess > 70% homology and the unrelated hagB and hagC family, that share 93% identity;The genes hagB and hagC are located close together on the chromosome.  Conservation of these two homologous genes in close proximity in the highly plastic genome of P. gingivalis suggests that possession of both genes is required for maximal fitness.
function_description: Required for adherence to oral epithelial cells; implicated in biofilm formation.

reference: VFG054342(gb|WP_039416961.1) (prtC) collagenase-like protease [PrtC (VF1448) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Porphyromonas gingivalis ATCC 33277]
characteristics: PrtC homologues shared by oralgut translocators showed similar domain organization compared with the P. gingivalis collagenase-encoding gene, characterized by a peptidase U32 domain followed by an additional peptidase U32 C-terminal domain.
function_description: Degrades human type I collagen, which is critical for structural tissue integrity; induces pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1alpha, IL-8 and TNF) and leads to tissue loss.

reference: VFG054356(gb|WP_005960619.1) (lktC) YbjN domain-containing protein [Leukotoxin (VF1459) - Exotoxin (VFC0235)] [Fusobacterium necrophorum strain SB057]
characteristics: Appears to be a major virulence factor and also a protective antigen of F. necrophorum; The operon consists of three genes (lktBAC) of which the second gene (lktA) is the leukotoxin structural gene. The LktB protein may be responsible for the secretion of the LktA protein while LktC protein does not show significant sequence similarity to proteins currently in the NCBI databases; The leukotoxin appears to be a novel protein and does not share sequence similarity with any other leukotoxin; The lktA leukotoxin gene ORF is 9726 bp, encoding a protein of 3241 amino acids with a molecular weight of 336,956 Da. The toxin is considerably greater in molecular weight than leukotoxins produced by other bacteria such as Mannheimia haemolytica (104,000 Da), Staphylococcus aureus (38,000 and 32,000 Da) and Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans (114,000 Da); The cytotoxicity appears to be specific to ruminant (cattle and sheep) and human neutrophils, but not those from pigs or rabbits and only moderately toxic to neutrophils of horses.
function_description: A high molecular weight secreted protein (330 kDa) that modulates the host immune system by activation of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMN) and induction of apoptosis in the bovine immune effector cells, and cytotoxic to ruminant PMN cells.

reference: VFG054376(gb|WP_029597751.1) (pduQ) iron-containing alcohol dehydrogenase [Pdu locus (VF1461) - Nutritional/Metabolic factor (VFC0272)] [Fusobacterium animalis strain KCOM 1325]
characteristics: Bacterial microcompartments are protein-based organelles that consist of metabolic enzymes encapsulated within a protein shell. Bacterial microcompartments increase reactions rates by creating high local concentrations of enzymes and substrates, confine pathway intermediates that are toxic or rapidly excreted from the cell, and enable the use of private cofactor pools; eut and pdu operons are broadly distributed within CRC associated lineage 1 (L1) of Fusobacterium species.
function_description: Enhances gastrointestinal niche adaptation by expanding metabolic capacity for 1,2-PD utilization while sequestering a toxic metabolic intermediate (propionaldehyde); triggers a virulence associated transcriptional program in bacteria, promoting adaptation to and persistence within extraoral niches such as CRC tumors.

reference: VFG054531(gb|WP_005902104.1) (cbpF) CEACAM-binding trimeric autotransporter adhesin CbpF [CbpF (VF1455) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: A homotrimeric type Vc autotransporter protein, in which all three protomers together form a trimeric passenger domain that remains exposed on the cell surface after expression, and a C-terminal beta-barrel domain that serves as a membrane anchor.
function_description: Mediates host cell attachment and suppresses antitumor immunity via binding to the carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule family, CEACAM1 and CEACAM5.

reference: VFG054532(gb|WP_106877174.1) (cmpA) autotransporter adhesin CmpA [CmpA (VF1458) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: NA
function_description: Critical for interspecies adherence and multispecies biofilm architecture.
mechanism: CmpA is the main molecule responsible for the specificity of the interaction between F. nucleatum and S. gordonii;plays a role in the coaggregation of F. nucleatum and another periodontal pathogen, Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans, through specific interactions with bacterial surface polysaccharides.

reference: VFG054533(gb|WP_005903511.1) (fadA) adhesion protein FadA [FadA (VF1449) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: Secreted via a Fap2-like autotransporter system and has amyloid-like properties under stress and disease conditions, which enhance its virulence;fadA deletion reduces bacterial binding to CHO and OKF6/Tert cells by 7080% and prevents bacterial translocation across the placental barrier; FadA is indispensable for tumorigenesis in vivo, as F. nucleatum FadA deletion mutants fail to induce colonic tumours in susceptible Apc Min/+ mice.
structure: An outer membrane protein with a small alpha-helical structure that is highly conserved in oral Fusobacteria;exists in both secreted form (12.6 kDa) and intact form (13.6 kDa). Membrane-anchored, intact, FadAotherwise termed preFadAconsists of 129 amino acid residues, whilst the secreted, mature FadA (mFadA) consists of only 111 amino acids, with mFadA being responsible for the adhesin's function. The mFadA monomer consists of two antiparallel alpha-helices connected by an 8-amino acid loop. Intramolecular and intermolecular leucine zipper motifs are present within and between mFadA molecules. Mutations introduced in the loop region (F68A, Y69A, K70A) or at key leucine zipper residues (Leu14 and Leu76) were shown to impair the ability of FadA to bind to various host cells; An active FadA complex (FadAc), composed of both mFadA and preFadA.
function_description: A crucial element in bacterial-host cell adhesion and invasion; mediates the microbial co-aggregation and facilitating the spread of bactera.
mechanism: A critical virulence factor binds to the 415534 region of vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-cadherin)on endothelial cells and to the extracellular domain 5 (EC5) of E-cadherins on epithelial cells, triggers inflammation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) via beta-catenin/NF-kappaB pathways, and aids in metastasis via junction disruption;binds to cadherin-11, a receptor protein in human pulmonary epithelial cells. This binding not only mediates bacterial adhesion and invasion, but also activates MAPK13/JUN inflammation pathways, leading to significant upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines including CSF3, TNF-alpha, CCL20, and TGF-beta.

reference: VFG054534(gb|WP_005902283.1) (fap2) galactose-inhibitable autotransporter adhesin Fap2 [Fap2 (VF1450) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: A type Va autotransporter OM protein and with about 400 kDa the largest single protein in F. nucleatum;  forms a ~45 nm long beta-helical rod-shaped extracellular domain (ECD) with the proposed interactions sites for its two receptors at the membrane-distal tip of the rod.
function_description: Fap2 binds Gal-GalNAc (D-galactose-beta(13)-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine) on CRC (colorectal cancer) cells and TIGIT (T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain) on NK cells, enhancing F. nucleatum colonization/adherence and inhibiting immune cytotoxicity.

reference: VFG054535(gb|WP_005902984.1) (fomA) major outer membrane protein FomA [FomA (VF1454) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: Non-specific porin FomA (42.4 kDa) is one of the most expressed outer membrane proteins (OMP), representing around 30% of such proteins.
function_description: A voltage-dependent general diffusion porin; acts as a receptor protein in co-aggregation with other oral pathogenic bacteria;promotes pro-inflammatory response by binding TLR2;The retention of FomA from extracellular vesicles from F. nucleatum (FnEVs) on the surface of CRC cells during membrane fusion between FnEVs and the recipient CRC cells facilitates the adhesion of F. nucleatum to CRC cells through its interaction with FN1441.

reference: VFG054536(gb|WP_005903112.1) (gbp) D-galactose-binding protein [Gbp (VF1456) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: NA
function_description: Promotes foam cell formation by interactsing with the Cyclophilin A (CypA) and CD147 and activating the NF-kappaB, MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling pathways; contributes to gastric cancer progression by a self-reinforcing CXCL8 signaling loop via the Gbp-CypA-NF-kappaB axis; disrupts osteogenic differentiation by inactivating the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway binding to ANXA2.

reference: VFG054537(gb|WP_005903789.1) (radD) autotransporter adhesin RadD [RadD (VF1451) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: A large autotransporter with molecular weight of 350 kDa.
function_description: Contributes to biofilm formation and promotes tumor colonization and progression, while undermining lymphocyte viability.
mechanism: Attaches to CD147 on cancer cells, which starts a pro-survival PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB pathway that helps the tumor grow and avoid the immune system; binds the inhibitory receptor Siglec-7 on NK cells, dampening their cytotoxic function and further enabling immune evasion;mediates the coaggregation of other oral microbes, including Streptococcus species (early colonisers) and Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola (late colonisers);binds to Flo9, the Candida  albicans' primary adhesins in the hyphal state, thereby synergistically promote colon tumor development and progression.

reference: VFG054538(gb|WP_106877227.1) (C4N14_RS10575) serine protease [Fusolisin (VF1462) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: Either remain cell-bound or be secreted, depending on the strain with varying enzymatic activity between strains. In most F. nucleatum strains, the 5565 kDa catalytic domain cleaves itself after crossing the membrane.
function_description: Functions as a serine protease not only involved in immune evasion but also likely plays a role in bacterial survival in multispecies environments like the oral cavity and potentially in the placenta where it is plausible that fusobacterial proliferation is fusolisin dependent.

reference: VFG054539(gb|WP_005904036.1) (eutS) ethanolamine utilization microcompartment protein EutS [Eut locus (VF1460) - Nutritional/Metabolic factor (VFC0272)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: Ethanolamine (H2N-CH2-CH2-OH) is a component of the membrane lipid phosphatidylethanolamine present in both eukaryotes and prokaryotesis a notable nutrient source to gut bacteria, such as Escherichia,  Salmonella,  and  Listeria;gut bacteria that possess the ethanolamine utilization (eut) operon have a significant advantage in this setting;The F. nucleatum genome harbors a conserved eut locus that encode several putative bacterial microcompartment (BMC) shell proteins and a two-component signal transduction system (TCS), in addition to the enzymes for ethanolamine transport and catabolism.
function_description: Upregulates the expression of virulence genes that help bacteria outcompete the host microbiota to establish a successful infection and the eutN mutant is defective in inducing preterm birth in a mouse model.

reference: VFG054556(gb|WP_005902929.1) (Fn-Dps) DNA starvation/stationary phase protection protein� [Fn-Dps  (VF1453) - Stress survival (VFC0282)] [Fusobacterium nucleatum subsp. nucleatum ATCC 23726]
characteristics: DNA hunger/stationary phase protective proteins (Dps) are bacterial ferritins that protect DNA from oxidative stress by preventing generation of hydroxyl radicals via the Fenton reaction; Dps protect DNA from oxidative stress by detoxifying H2O2 and have been implicated in intracellular survival and virulence such as Campylobacter jejuni and Listeria monocytogenes. Moreover, the Dps from two obligate anaerobes Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) and B. fragilis, were found to play an important role in the protection of cells from peroxide stress, and increase the survival of Pg inside endothelial cells.
structure: a dodecameric protein consisting of 17 kDa monomers with a central cavity where ferrous ions bind.
function_description: Lyses and disrupts erythrocytes, enhances intracellular survival of F. nucleatum in macrophages, and promotes CRC metastasis; binds to the PD-L1 gene promoter activating transcription factor-3 (ATF3) to upregulate PD-L1 expression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cells, thereby to counteract immune attack and protect both intracellular F. nucleatum and host cells.

reference: VFG054571(gb|WP_005540930.1) (cdtA) cytolethal distending toxin subunit Aa-CdtA [Aa-CDT (VF1308) - Exotoxin (VFC0235)] [Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans strain 4S]
characteristics: Cdts represent a highly distributed and conserved family of putative virulence factors produced by more than 30 gamma- and epsilon-Proteobacteria. These include: Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans, an oral pathogen,  Haemophilus ducreyi, a genital pathogen, as well as diarrheal disease-causing gastric pathogens such as Campylobacter jejuni, and some Escherichia coli isolates. Aa is the only known oral bacterial species capable of producing CDT (Aa-CDT), which is expressed in most of its serotypes;  Cdt, a heterotrimeric holotoxin typically functions as an AB2 toxin where CdtB is the active (A) unit and the complex of CdtA and CdtC comprise the binding (B) unit; belonging to the group of cyclomodulins.
function_description: A tripartite toxin composed of three subunits: CdtA, CdtB, and CdtC. The active subunit, CdtB, has DNase activity and enters host cells, where it causes DNA damage. This leads to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis;  Aa-CDT also induces genomic instability in oral epithelial cells, potentially contributing to the development of cancer.
mechanism: CdtB is the enzymatically active subunit, with DNase I and phosphatidylinositol-3, 4, 5-triphosphate (PIP3) phosphatase activity, while CdtA and CdtC subunits bind to cholesterol in the host cell

gene_id: membrane, facilitating the internalisation of CdtB to exert its effects within the host cell;In the oral cavity, Aa-CDT induces apoptosis, cell cycle arrest, and damage in fibroblasts and gingival epithelial cells, promoting bacterial invasion. Additionally, Aa-CDT stimulates RANKL (receptor activator of NF-kappaB ligand) production in gingival fibroblasts and T lymphocytes, a key effector of alveolar bone resorption in periodontitis.

reference: VFG054580(gb|WP_148326169.1) (emaA) trimeric autotransporter adhesin EmaA [EmaA (VF1467) - Adherence (VFC0001)] [Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans strain 4S]
vf_full_name: Extracellular matrix binding protein adhesin A
characteristics: Trimeric autotransporter adhesins encompass a wide range of monomer sizes, including YadA (42 kDa), UspA1 (83kDa), UspA2 (60 kDa), Hia (114 kDa) and BadA (340 kDa);  In contrast to YadA, UspA1/UspA2, and BadA, which are expressed at high densities on the bacterial surface, EmaA is sparsely distributed on the surface and can be more easily found at the apical end of the bacterium; Seven serotypes (af) have been identified for A. actinomycetemcomitans. Serotypes b and c express the cognate full-length isoform (b-EmaA, 202 kDa monomers), whereas serotypes a and d express an intermediate isoform, which is a shorter variant of EmaA containing a 279-amino-acid deletion (a-EmaA, 173 kDa monomers). Both molecular isoforms of the protein bind to collagen;EmaA is a glycoprotein modified with the sugars associated with the O-antigen. An O-antigen ligase (waaL) is required for the collagen-binding activity associated with EmaA.
structure: The prototypical EmaA structure consists of three identical subunits, assembled on the bacterial outer membrane, which form antenna-like structures of 35 nm in diameter, projecting at least 150 nm away from the bacterial surface;  The antenna-like structure is composed of multiple domains, including an ellipsoidal-shaped head domain at the distal end of the structure, and a long stalk, which is connected to a flexible neck region;  The collagen-binding activity is attributed to the head domain, which corresponds to amino acids 57627 of the monomer and encompasses the most apical 30 nm of the antennae-like structures.
function_description: EmaA, the largest autotransporter protein of A. actinomycetemcomitans, required for collagen binding, biofilm formation, and cell-to-cell interaction.
mechanism: The EmaA/collagen interaction agrees more closely with the model proposed for the binding of YadA to collagen. In this model, the interaction is governed by the electrostatic forces between the collagen fibrils and the charged residues of the trimeric YadA surface.

reference: VFG054581(gb|WP_041915477.1) (dspB) glycoside hydrolase dispersin B [DspB (VF1468) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans strain 4S]

function_description: Inhibits biofilm and pellicle formation; detaches preformed biofilms and disaggregates bacterial flocs; sensitizes preformed biofilms to detachment by enzymes, detergents, and metal chelators, and sensitizes preformed biofilms to killing by antiseptics, antibiotics, bacteriophages, macrophages, and predatory bacteria.

reference: VFG055001(gb|NP_216364.1) (ureA) urease subunit gamma [Urease (VF1478) - Enzyme (VFC0251)] [Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv]
characteristics: Urease is absent from humans and is considered an attractive target for the development of antibacterial and antifungal drugs.
function_description: Urease converts urea to ammonia and carbamate, for an alkalizing effect or as a nitrogen source. Mtb urease has an alkalizing effect in macrophages and plays a role in the central metabolism of bacteria by providing a source of nitrogen; Mtb protein UreC functions as a host DNA repair inhibitor that activates the type-I IFN pathway to promote lipid droplets and the intracellular survival of Mtb.
mechanism: UreC inhibits host DNA repair by interacting with RuvB-like protein 2 (RUVBL2) and impeding the formation of the RUVBL1-RUVBL2-RAD51 DNA repair complex. The suppression of this repair pathway increases the abundance of micronuclei that trigger the cyclic GMPAMP synthase (cGAS)/stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway and subsequent interferon-beta (IFN-beta) production. UreC-mediated activation of the IFN-beta pathway upregulates the expression of SR-A1 to form lipid droplets that facilitate Mtb replication. Thus Mtb triggers a cascade of cellular events that establish a nutrient-rich replicative niche.
